chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Mukhtār, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

Concerning the believer’s ʿawrah being forbidden to another believer, he said: “It is not that it is uncovered and you see something of him; rather, it is that you disparage him or find fault with him.”

key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِ: the believer, whose dignity and sanctity are protected
key_terms.تَزْرِيَ: to disparage, belittle, or speak slightingly of someone
key_terms.تَعِيبَهُ: to criticize him or attribute faults to him
key_terms.عَوْرَةِ: the vulnerable or private aspect whose violation is forbidden

ai.seo_question: What does the prohibition of a believer’s ʿawrah mean in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the sanctity of a believer’s ʿawrah is not limited to physical exposure. Its deeper meaning here is the prohibition of belittling, disgracing, or faulting a fellow believer, emphasizing moral and social inviolability.
